extracted.intended_audience: empirical accounting/finance researchers studying IPOs, firm disclosure, and communication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical measurement standards for defining, constructing, and using press-release variables around IPO quiet-periods and for analyzing their relation to stock return synchronicity and volatility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are defined as Factiva articles with a newswire listed as the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Appendix A for specific sources designated as newswires and further details on the construction of the press release variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement window around quiet period (day 0)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plots and analyses use the quiet period expiration date defined as day 0; figures plot the mean number of press releases firms issue in the days surrounding the quiet period expiration date (day 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphs show days before and after quiet expiration (e.g., −10 to +10 shown in figures); press-release counts are aggregated by day relative to the quiet expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiet-period and post-quiet measurement windows (25-day standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPOs with a 25-day quiet period (pre-Global Settlement) measure quiet-period synchronicity/volatility using daily returns during the quiet period. For IPOs with a 40-day quiet period (post-Global Settlement) measure quiet-period synchronicity/volatility using daily returns for the first 25 days of the quiet period. For all IPOs measure post-quiet period synchronicity/volatility using daily returns for the first 25 days after the expiration of the quiet period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press-release variables tied to these same windows: quiet period press releases (first 25 days in quiet) and post-quiet press releases (first 25 days after expiration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release activity variables (counts and differences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm communication activity is summarized with Quiet period press releases, Post-quiet press releases, and Δ Press releases (the change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables report mean, st. dev., percentiles for these variables (e.g., Quiet period press releases mean = 3.65, Post-quiet = 5.30, Δ = +1.65). Δ Press releases is used as a primary measure of change in firm press-release activity around quiet expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of factiva/newswire indicator (source-based inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Factiva articles that list a newswire as the source are treated as press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A enumerates which Factiva sources are designated as newswires; this choice restricts press-release counts to newswire-distributed items (excludes non-newswire items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation choice: daily mean press-release plotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures plot the mean number of press releases firms issue in the days surrounding the quiet period expiration date (day 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical presentation uses per-day means (and separate lines for IPO vs matched control firms) to visualize temporal patterns before and after quiet expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent variable in regressions: Δ Log press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Multivariate regressions use Δ Log press releases as the dependent variable in analyses of press-release determinants (Table 3 Panel B shows 'Dependent variable = Δ Log press releases').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regression models include many firm controls; coefficients and t-statistics presented. Log transformation and differencing are used to reduce skew and focus on proportional changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling press-release impact on synchronicity: Δ Log press release (and interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel A regresses the change in stock return synchronicity on the change in press release activity (Δ Log press release), information environment variables, interactive terms, and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interactive terms include Δ Log press release × Log MVE, × High R&D, × Underpricing, × Log analyst coverage. Panel B repeats analyses using IPO firm's change in synchronicity relative to matched control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matched control selection for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Matched control firms are existing public firms in the same industry with the closest market capitalization at the time of quiet period expiration, and have been trading for at least one years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control firms' synchronicity and volatility measures are computed over the same windows as their corresponding IPO firms to enable within-sample and relative comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample inclusion / exclusion rules for IPO sample
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPO sample consists of U.S. firms which completed an offering from January 1, 1996 through December 31, 2011. Exclude unit offerings, American Depositary Receipts, spin-offs, reverse leveraged buy-outs, closed-end funds, real estate investment trusts, and any IPO consisting of non-common shares. Eliminate firms that were already trading at the time of IPO, and firms without corresponding Compustat gvkey or CRSP permno identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also exclude firms with no other firms in the same 2-digit industry (needed to compute synchronicity). These selection choices determine the final sample of 3,380 IPOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance reporting convention
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbols •••, ••, and • represent significance at the 1%, 5%, and 10% levels, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used consistently across tables and panels to flag statistical significance of means and regression coefficients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronicity and volatility construction dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Synchronicity and volatility calculations are referred to in Table 4 and Appendix A; synchronicity and volatility measures for control firms are measured over the same windows as their corresponding IPO firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper ties press-release variables to these market-measured outcomes (Δ Synchronicity, Δ volatility) and uses them as dependent variables when testing the effect of press releases on return behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operationalization of press-release effect tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests regress the change in stock return synchronicity on press-release changes, information environment variables, interactive terms, and standard controls (e.g., Log MVE, High R&D, Underpricing, Log analyst coverage, Δ Volume, Δ Log σ, offer price, underwriter rank, days in registration, age at IPO, BM, H-index, retained interest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables present coefficients, t-statistics and R-squared; multiple specifications shown (within sample and relative-to-control). Inclusion of controls and fixed interactions is part of the empirical standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction note: using first 25 days for 40-day quiet periods
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPOs which have a 40-day quiet period (post-Global Settlement), quiet-period measures use daily returns for the first 25 days of the quiet period (rather than the full 40).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This harmonization (using first 25 days) is used to make quiet-period measures comparable across pre- and post-Global Settlement IPOs.
